title: Zariski gluing of separated finitely presented isomorphism graph representatives
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes and $X\to S$, $Y\to S$ separated morphisms [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, write $X_T=X\times_ST$, $Y_T=Y\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and let $F(T)=\operatorname{Isom}_T(X_T,Y_T)$, with transition maps the canonical pullbacks of isomorphisms. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed open cover of $S$. Suppose that for each $i$ there is a separated finitely presented $U_i$-scheme $J_i$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], together with bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{U_i}(T,J_i)\simeq F(T)$ for every $T\to U_i$, natural in all $U_i$-morphisms of test schemes. Assume these bijections identify a point with the closed graph $D\subset X_T\times_TY_T$ of its isomorphism: both projections $p_X:D\to X_T$, $p_Y:D\to Y_T$ are invertible, the associated map is $p_Y\circ p_X^{-1}$, and every such closed subscheme gives exactly one point [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $F$ is a Zariski sheaf: compatible isomorphisms on any open cover of $T$ glue uniquely, including their inverses. The subfunctor $F_i\subset F$ consisting of elements for which $T\to S$ factors through $U_i$ is represented by $J_i$ as an $S$-scheme; its inclusion is representable by the open immersion $T\times_SU_i\hookrightarrow T$ after pullback by any element of $F(T)$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. There is a separated finitely presented $S$-scheme $J$ representing $F$, with natural representing isomorphisms $J\times_SU_i\simeq J_i$. The overlap identifications and the global representing bijection preserve the closed graphs and the formula $p_Y\circ p_X^{-1}$ in both directions. For every morphism $S'\to S$, the pullback $J\times_SS'$ represents $T\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_T((X\times_SS')\times_{S'}T,(Y\times_SS')\times_{S'}T)$ on $S'$-schemes, with exactly the same graphs and inverse projection formula. Here finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The cover need not be finite, and there is no Noetherian hypothesis on $S$, $S'$ or any test scheme.

source.place: Tag 01JB (lemma-glue), gluing scheme morphisms and inverse identities; Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), open-subfunctor representability; moduli-curves.tex Tag 0DSQ (lemma-curves-diagonal-separated-fp), target-local separatedness and finite presentation. This is parent proof steps 7, 8 and 9 with the local graph representatives as hypotheses.

proof.text: Let $T=\bigcup_a V_a$ and let $f_a:X_{V_a}\simeq Y_{V_a}$ be compatible isomorphisms. The schemes $X_{V_a}$ and $Y_{V_a}$ are the inverse-image open covers of $X_T$ and $Y_T$: identify the relevant pullbacks by their universal properties, and apply base change of open immersions. Regard the $f_a$ as maps into $Y_T$ and glue them by morphism gluing to $f:X_T\to Y_T$. The inverses agree on overlaps, since the inverse of a fixed isomorphism is unique, so they similarly glue to $g:Y_T\to X_T$. The composites $gf$ and $fg$ restrict to identities on these covers; morphism uniqueness makes them identities globally. The structure-map equality making $f$ a $T$-map is also checked on the cover. The same uniqueness proves uniqueness of the glued isomorphism. Thus $F$ is a Zariski sheaf, including for the empty test scheme.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), mapping property for maps out; 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion).

proof.text: For a test $T\to S$, an $S$-map $T\to J_i$ can exist only if $T\to S$ factors through $U_i$. Such a factorization is unique, since an open subscheme inclusion is a monomorphism (a map into its open ringed subspace has its underlying map and sheaf map uniquely prescribed). In that case $S$-maps to $J_i$ are precisely $U_i$-maps, so the given bijection represents $F_i$. Given $\xi\in F(T)$, the fibre product $h_T\times_F F_i$ evaluated at $R/S$ consists exactly of maps $h:R\to T$ whose composite to $S$ factors through $U_i$; the second component must be $h^*\xi$. The fibre-product universal property identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}_S(R,T\times_SU_i)$. Its projection is the base change of $U_i\hookrightarrow S$, hence open. The opens $T_i=T\times_SU_i$ cover $T$, and $\xi|_{T_i}\in F_i(T_i)$, proving the covering assertion.

Put $U_{ij}=U_i\cap U_j$ and $J_{ij}=J_i\times_{U_i}U_{ij}$. For every $T/U_{ij}$ the fibre-product universal property and the given natural bijections identify both $\operatorname{Hom}_{U_{ij}}(T,J_{ij})$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{U_{ij}}(T,J_{ji})$ with $F(T)$. Their composite is a natural bijection, hence Yoneda full faithfulness gives an isomorphism $\theta_{ij}:J_{ij}\simeq J_{ji}$. It is characterized by preserving the classified isomorphism. The reverse transformation is its inverse. On triple intersections $\theta_{jk}\theta_{ij}$ and $\theta_{ik}$ induce the same map on every test point, namely the identity on its element of $F(T)$; faithfulness gives the cocycle identity. Likewise $\theta_{ii}=1$. These checks use no choice of coordinates or a finite subcover.

source.place: Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), construction of overlap isomorphisms and verification of their cocycle; categories.tex Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Apply scheme gluing along the base open cover to the schemes $J_i/U_i$ and the isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}$ just constructed. Its hypotheses are exactly the identity and triple-intersection equalities from the previous step. This gives an $S$-scheme $J$ with $J\times_SU_i\simeq J_i$, compatible with $\theta_{ij}$. The induced maps $j_i:J_i\to J$ identify $J_i$ with the inverse-image opens of $U_i$: they are pullbacks of $U_i\hookrightarrow S$. In particular they are open immersions and their images cover $J$.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue) and 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes); relative gluing as stated by lem-galois-glue.

proof.text: Let $u_i\in F(J_i)$ correspond to $1_{J_i}$. By naturality and the definition of $\theta_{ij}$, $u_i|_{J_{ij}}=\theta_{ij}^*u_j$. The sheaf property proved in step 1 glues them to $u\in F(J)$. Define $\beta_T(a)=a^*u$ for an $S$-map $a:T\to J$. Given $\xi\in F(T)$, on $T_i=T\times_SU_i$ the local representing bijection gives a unique map $a_i:T_i\to J_i$. On $T_i\cap T_j$ the maps factor into $J_{ij},J_{ji}$ and satisfy $a_j=\theta_{ij}a_i$, because they classify the same restriction of $\xi$. Their composites with $j_i,j_j$ agree, so morphism gluing produces $a:T\to J$ and gives $a^*u=\xi$ by step 1. Conversely any such $a$ must restrict to these unique local maps, because $J_i=J\times_SU_i$; morphism uniqueness proves uniqueness of $a$. Finally $(ah)^*u=h^*(a^*u)$ for every $h:T'\to T$, so $\beta$ is natural and restricts to the prescribed bijections on $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), last two proof paragraphs: universal element and unique representing morphism.

proof.text: The restriction of $J\to S$ over $U_i$ is $J_i\to U_i$, which is separated and locally of finite presentation by hypothesis. Target-open locality gives these two properties for $J\to S$. Every $J_i\to U_i$ is also quasi-compact, since it is of finite presentation; target-open locality of quasi-compactness therefore gives quasi-compactness of $J\to S$. Since a separated morphism is quasi-separated, $J\to S$ is quasi-separated. Thus it is of finite presentation in precisely the stated sense: locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Neither target-locality statement requires the cover to be finite or $S$ to be quasi-compact or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize); schemes.tex Tag 01KK (definition-separated), paragraph following it; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), clause (6).

proof.text: For an isomorphism $f\in F(T)$, the projection $X_T\times_TY_T\to X_T$ is the base change of $Y\to S$ along $X_T\to S$, using the fibre-product universal property. It is separated. Its section $(1,f):X_T\to X_T\times_TY_T$ is therefore a closed immersion. This is the closed graph $\Gamma_f$; its projections are $1_{X_T}$ and $f$, so it has both projections invertible. Conversely, if a closed subscheme $j:D\hookrightarrow X_T\times_TY_T$ has invertible projections $p_X,p_Y$, then $f=p_Yp_X^{-1}$ is an isomorphism and $j p_X^{-1}=(1,f)$ by equality of the two product projections. Thus $D$ and $\Gamma_f$ are the same closed subobject, with the asserted inverse formula. On each $U_i$ the bijections use exactly this graph by hypothesis. Step 3 preserves $f$, and step 5 restricts to the given bijections, so both the overlap identifications and $\beta$ preserve these graphs in both directions.

source.place: Tags 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), clause (3), and 01KT (lemma-section-immersion); Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), matching of the universal elements.

proof.text: Fix any $S'\to S$ and any $T/S'$. The fibre-product universal property gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{S'}(T,J\times_SS')\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,J)$. Compose with $\beta_T$. The same universal property identifies $(X\times_SS')\times_{S'}T$ with $X\times_ST$, and likewise for $Y$, so the result is exactly the required isomorphism set on $S'$. All identifications preserve projections and are natural in $T$. For a further test change $h:T'\to T$, the pullback of $(1,f)$ is $(1,h^*f)$ by its two projections, and it is closed by base change of closed immersions. Pullback preserves composition and identities, so $(h^*p_X)h^*(p_X^{-1})=1$ and $h^*(p_X^{-1})(h^*p_X)=1$; uniqueness of inverse gives $h^*(p_X^{-1})=(h^*p_X)^{-1}$. Consequently $h^*(p_Yp_X^{-1})=(h^*p_Y)(h^*p_X)^{-1}$. This proves the claimed arbitrary-base-change graph and inverse-formula compatibility without imposing a finiteness condition on $h$ or $S'$.
